entries.note: He raises a possibility and explicitly withholds a firm prediction.

entries.test: Public financial reports and industry revenue estimates would establish whether generative AI had generated hundreds of billions of dollars by August 14, 2023.
entries.note: The lower estimates are probabilistic, but 'certainly not hundreds of billions' supplies a firm, testable ceiling.

entries.test: Published investment totals and cumulative revenue estimates for autonomous driving and the driver-assistance businesses he includes would establish their magnitude and disparity through August 2023.
entries.note: His scope explicitly includes driver-assistance software and Tesla upcharges.

entries.test: OpenAI's publicly documented cash reserves, financing commitments, revenue and expenses around August 2023 would establish whether it faced imminent financial distress while retaining longer-term financial risks.
entries.note: The proposition removes his 'I don’t think' framing and presents his assessment as categorical.

entries.test: Longitudinal programmer adoption surveys and coding-assistant usage data would show whether generative AI remains an enduring coding tool or programmers broadly abandon it.
entries.note: The plain reading concerns durable adoption by programmers collectively, not every individual programmer.
He explicitly attributes this assessment to Malik and adopts it. The central cost-coverage and bankruptcy assessments are probabilistic.
'I am doubtful' expresses likelihood rather than a firm commitment.
'Will probably' explicitly qualifies the operating-cost prediction.

entries.test: Contemporaneous revenue and operating-cost disclosures, application adoption data, and chat-search accuracy evaluations would test the stated commercial and performance assessments.
entries.note: The proposition drops 'appears' and 'perhaps,' and removes the explicit chat-search exception to 'no killer app.'

entries.test: Public technical disclosures, independent reproductions, competing products and documented barriers to entry as of August 2023 would test copyability and evidence for durable competitive protection.
entries.note: The proposition broadens 'most of the basic technology' and drops 'to a large degree.'

entries.test: Reproducible model stability evaluations and documented integration failures would show whether unpredictable or changing outputs impede reliable product engineering.
entries.note: The surrounding text gives 'unstable' a concrete meaning: unpredictable correctness and changing answers.
The central relationship is causal, and 'can even change' becomes the firmer 'change over time.' The claim of insuperable difficulty remains explicitly a possibility.
The proposition omits people leaving as part of the antecedent and changes deceleration into decline. 'Could' makes the predicted spiral a possibility.
The source says only some of the same people fled crypto; 'as they did crypto' broadens that attribution. The prospective departure is qualified by 'might.'

entries.test: Contemporaneous productivity studies, advertising results, autonomous-driving safety records, diagnostic evaluations and chat-search accuracy tests would establish performance and reliability in the named uses.
entries.note: These are practical performance claims with public tests, despite the evaluative phrasing.
The proposition turns 'seem to be predicated' into an unqualified assertion. Whether valuations are justified is expressly left uncertain.
Neither the apparent robustness nor the degree of actual robustness has a shared evidentiary benchmark.
